ov: A one-toed, hoofed grazer, domesticated on the steppes of western Eurasia. Modern breeds spread across Eurasia from about 2000 BCE, and horses have been ridden and worked ever since.

why.et: Horse meat is eaten in many parts of the world. About 5 million horses are slaughtered for meat each year.
why.dg: A frightened horse's first instinct is to run; if it can't, it bites, kicks, strikes out or rears.
why.p: Kept for riding, sport and work more than as pets.

ht: 142–163 cm at the shoulder (light riding horses)
rg: Worldwide with people, plus feral herds descended from domestic horses. These are not true wild horses.
df: Grass and other plants. Horses are grazers, with front teeth adapted to biting off grass.

cf.tip: A pony is a horse that stands no taller than 14.2 hands (147 cm) at the withers. Anything taller counts as a horse.
A donkey has much larger ears, which help it pick up distant sounds and cool its blood.

fx: Horses can doze standing up, using a “stay apparatus” in their legs, but they must lie down to reach REM sleep.
